einzeiler: The life, plays, and revolutionary activism of French writer Olympe de Gouges
kurzfassung: Olympe de Gouges was a prolific French playwright and political activist during the 18th century. She is best known for her 1791 work, Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen. Despite her contributions to early feminist thought and abolitionism, she was executed by guillotine during the French Revolution.
stichpunkte: Born Marie Gouze in southern France in 1748 before moving to Paris and adopting the pen name Olympe de Gouges
Authored numerous plays tackling social injustices, including the pioneering abolitionist play The Slavery of Negroes
Faced unique gender-based pushback and arrest threats from the monopolistic Comédie-Française over her play submissions
Published the Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen in 1791 in response to male-centric revolutionary documents
Advocated for broad reforms including divorce rights, the end of the death penalty, and legal protections for children born out of wedlock
Held pro-monarchy views, offered to defend Louis XVI at his treason trial, and criticized the radicalizing revolution
Arrested for proposing regional self-governance and executed by guillotine in November 1793
Suffered decades of historical vilification before gaining recognition as a key forerunner of the feminist movement in the late 20th century

kapitel.titel: The Comédie-Française and The Slavery of Negroes
Political Activism and the French Revolution
Declaration of the Rights of Woman

clips.hook: Writing through a secretary due to regional dialects and minimal schooling
clips.text: Because her primary spoken language was a regional dialect and her formal schooling was limited, she relied on a secretary to write down her French texts.

clips.hook: The stark gender disparity in French theater productions
clips.text: National theater regulations mandated the production of numerous new plays annually, yet works written by women constituted an extremely minute fraction of the actual repertoire.

clips.hook: Dozens of plays and political pamphlets produced during her lifetime
clips.text: She authored over forty dramatic works alongside more than sixty political pamphlets throughout the turbulent revolutionary period.

clips.hook: Reclaiming equality through the first article on women's rights
clips.text: The foundational article of the new declaration established that women enter the world free and maintain rights equal to men, permitting social distinctions solely based on collective welfare.

clips.hook: Defiant behavior and assumed age during her tribunal appearance
clips.text: During courtroom proceedings where legal counsel was denied, she misstated her age and reacted to the accusations with conspicuous physical gestures of disbelief and detachment.

beschreibung:
This 2021 episode covers Olympe de Gouges, known primarily for her 1791 pamphlet “Declaration of the Rights of Woman and the Citizen.” But her writing and political activity went far beyond that one pamphlet.
